references.text: The question of the value of gaining the world at the cost of one's soul is reflected in Isaiah's warning against spending resources on what does not give true life.
This verse reflects the idea that material gains cannot be compared to the value of one's relationship with God, which is also a theme in the book of Psalms.
Jesus asks a similar question in Matthew, emphasizing the consequences of valuing material things over spiritual well-being.
Luke gives a parallel to Mark by highlighting the futility of gaining the world if it leads to the loss of one's soul.
